item.title: Reps pass FCT rent regulation bill amid disagreement
item.description: Lawmakers divided over proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to regulate rental payments and curb exploitative practices by landlords and estate agents in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), amid disagreements among lawmakers over a proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments. The bill, sponsored by Rep. Paul Sunday Nnamchi, seeks to regulate advance rent payments, arbitrary rent increases and agency fees, as well as establish a unified digital register for housing agents. It also provides safeguards for landlords and tenants, with penalties for violations of its provisions. Leading the debate, Nnamchi said the rising cost of accommodation and excessive demands for advance rent had placed enormous financial pressure on residents, affecting household savings, small businesses and employment mobility. He said the proposed legislation was designed to establish a fairer and more accountable rental system through the regulation of advance payments, reasonable limits on agency fees and proper identification of housing agents. “Mr Speaker, this legislation is not intended to undermine property rights or discourage investment. Rather, it recognises that legitimate commercial interests must coexist with public protection. Landlords deserve reasonable returns. “Agents deserve professional recognition. And tenants deserve fairness and protection from exploitation,” he said. Supporting the bill, Rep. Idris Zacharias, representing Ida/Igalamela/Ibaji/Ofu Federal Constituency of Kogi State, described the proposal as important but called for broader consideration of land administration and housing challenges in the FCT. He also urged the House Committee on FCT and Area Councils to be included in the committee that would consider the bill. Similarly, Rep. Chinedu Ogah, representing Ikwo/Ezza South Federal Constituency of Ebonyi State, backed the proposal, citing the difficulties businesses face in securing office accommodation in Abuja. Ogah said renting a three-bedroom office in Wuse could cost between N25 million and N30 million annually, excluding additional agency charges. He argued that regulating the rental market would provide clearer rules for transactions and encourage investment in the sector. However, Rep. Leko Jafaru Gambo, representing Bogoro/Dass/Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency of Bauchi State, called for a review of the bill’s title, arguing that the word “prohibit” should be replaced with “regulate”. He also suggested that the legislation should have nationwide application, but Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu clarified that its current scope was limited to the FCT. Rep. Ibe Okwara Osonwa, representing Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency of Abia State, also supported regulation but cautioned against an outright prohibition of multi-year rent arrangements. item.title: Google gives Nigerian health-tech firm $2.5m for maternal care AI
item.description: Project targets 1.9m women in four states By Juliet Umeh Google has awarded Nigerian health technology company, Helium Health, a $2.5 million (about N3.4 billion) grant to deploy artificial intelligence (AI) tools aimed at improving maternal healthcare in Nigeria. The company was the only Nigerian organisation among 15 global recipients selected for the $30 million Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation, an initiative supporting organisations using technology to improve public services in partnership with governments. The Nigerian project was unveiled in Lagos during an executive briefing with Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, led by executives of Google and Helium Health. The initiative will be implemented in Lagos, Delta, Kano and Oyo states, with Lagos serving as its primary launchpad. The selected organisations will also participate in a Google.org accelerator programme, where they will receive technical support from Google engineers and artificial intelligence product experts. Speaking on the grant, Helium Health Chief Executive Officer, Dimeji Sofowora, said the company had spent the past decade developing technology and partnerships to improve healthcare delivery across Africa. He said its maternal health initiatives had already reached more than 3.5 million women, adding that the Google.org support would enable the company to expand its interventions and extend access to quality maternal healthcare. “Through our maternal health initiatives, we’ve already reached over 3.5 million women, and Google.org’s support gives us an opportunity to build on that foundation, scale what works, and reach even more women with quality maternal healthcare,” he said. The company’s Head of Public Health, Dr Shona Oluwatola, said the project aims to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years and contribute to a 30 per cent reduction in maternal mortality. She noted that Nigeria accounts for nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths globally, stressing the need for interventions that would help women identify pregnancy-related risks early and access timely medical attention. “Nigeria accounts for nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths globally. Behind every maternal death is a woman whose family expected her to come home,” Oluwatola said. “Our goal is to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years and contribute to a 30 per cent reduction in maternal mortality,” she added. The project will deploy Helium Health’s HeliumMum platform to help pregnant women identify potential health risks early and access appropriate medical care. The platform will connect pregnant women with healthcare providers through electronic medical records and AI-powered clinical decision-support tools, while providing governments with data to guide maternal health policies and service delivery. item.title: I’ll end insecurity, hunger, make Nigeria affordable — Atiku, launches campaign
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to tackle insecurity, hunger and the rising cost of living if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Atiku made the pledge on Wednesday in a statement posted on his X platform while announcing the launch of his presidential campaign in Sokoto State. The former Vice-President said Nigerians were tired of hunger, fear and what he described as broken promises, adding that his campaign would offer a plan to address the country’s challenges. “Sokoto, I am here! I am deeply grateful for the rousing welcome as I formally launch my campaign for the presidency from this historic seat of faith, scholarship, and leadership,” he said. He pledged to end insecurity across the country, restore hope to young people and make Nigeria affordable again. “Nigerians are tired of hunger, fear, and broken promises. Today, they have a choice, a plan, and a leader ready to deliver. I will end the insecurity that haunts our communities, restore hope to our young people, and make Nigeria affordable again,” Atiku said. He described the Sokoto campaign launch as the beginning of what he called a journey to rescue Nigeria, urging supporters to unite behind his presidential ambition. “The journey to rescue Nigeria begins here. Together, we will win,” he added. The post I’ll end insecurity, hunger, make Nigeria affordable — Atiku, launches campaign appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate to suspend bills for new universities in line with FG policy
item.description: The Senate has directed its committees and the Clerk to suspend the processing of bills seeking the establishment of new universities and other tertiary institutions, in line with the Federal Government’s policy. Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, announced the directive during plenary on Wednesday, urging lawmakers to respect the government’s decision to halt the establishment of additional tertiary institutions. Bamidele said the policy was aimed at strengthening existing universities and other institutions before considering the creation of new ones. He urged the Clerk of the Senate to inform lawmakers about the directive and advised relevant committees, particularly those on education, against presenting bills for new institutions for consideration. He acknowledged that lawmakers sometimes found it difficult to reject requests from colleagues seeking support for the establishment of universities and other tertiary institutions. Supporting the directive, Senate President Godswill Akpabio said President Bola Tinubu had discussed the matter with the leadership of the National Assembly and expressed opposition to establishing new universities, polytechnics and other tertiary institutions for the next five to seven years. According to Akpabio, the moratorium would give existing institutions time to develop their infrastructure and commence effective academic operations. He noted that some recently established universities existed largely on paper, with several yet to acquire permanent sites or complete necessary site-clearance processes. The Senate President stressed that establishing a university was a major national responsibility, noting that such institutions should not be created with the same ease as primary schools. He added that universities were national institutions expected to admit students from across the country, regardless of their geographical locations. Akpabio said the Federal Government had made efforts to ensure the geographical spread of universities across the country, making it important to consolidate existing investments. He consequently directed the Clerk to ensure that bills seeking the establishment of new tertiary institutions were no longer listed for consideration. The Senate adjourned plenary until November 10, 2026, at 11 a.m. (NAN) The post Senate to suspend bills for new universities in line with FG policy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: ADC urges Nigerians to replicate US voters’ revolt against ruling party
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has urged Nigerians to take a cue from American voters by using the 2027 general elections to reject the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, over economic hardship, worsening insecurity and declining living standards. The party said Tuesday’s US midterm elections had demonstrated that no government could take voters for granted, insisting that Nigerians must put their welfare above political loyalty, sentiments and personality politics when deciding who governs them. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the American election outcome as a decisive rebuke of the ruling Republican Party’s leadership and economic policies, saying it offered an important lesson for Nigeria’s democracy. “Americans have shown that when politicians become arrogant, when policies punish ordinary people, and when those in power mistake popularity for a permanent licence to govern, the ballot box remains the ultimate instrument of accountability,” the party said. The opposition party said Nigerians had endured years of economic hardship and worsening insecurity under the President Bola Tinubu-led APC administration, questioning why the ruling party should be rewarded with another mandate. “We cannot continue to complain about the cost of living while voting for a President who has made life unaffordable. We cannot demand security while rewarding failure. We cannot earnestly yearn for change while sustaining the very political system responsible for our collective impoverishment,” the ADC said. Urging Nigerians to mobilise ahead of 2027, the party called for massive voter turnout, describing the Permanent Voter Card as an instrument for changing the country’s political direction. “History beckons in 2027. Our voters’ cards must become instruments of change, not souvenirs of citizenship. Nigerians must turn out massively and vote for their own interests,” Abdullahi said. The party also unveiled its campaign message, presenting itself and its candidates as an alternative to the APC-led government. “The ADC and its candidates are offering Nigerians a clear alternative: Make Nigeria Affordable Again. Make Nigeria Safe Again. Give Nigerians Jobs Again,” the statement said. Drawing a direct parallel with the American elections, Abdullahi urged Nigerians to make their votes count in 2027, warning that the APC should not mistake its hold on power for a permanent mandate. “If Americans can use their votes to demand better, Nigerians can do the same. In 2027, let our votes speak louder than the APC-induced suffering,” he said. The post 2027: ADC urges Nigerians to replicate US voters’ revolt against ruling party appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Photos: ADC supporters rally in large numbers for campaign flag-off in Sokoto
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The slogan “Tinubu Must Go” reverberated across the venue of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign flag-off along Illorin Road in Sokoto metropolis on Wednesday, as supporters of the opposition party expressed their opposition to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration ahead of the 2027 general elections. The slogan, which became a recurring chant among the crowd, reflected the determination of ADC supporters to mobilise Nigerians for political change and challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) at the polls. The chant gained momentum as supporters, many of whom had travelled from different parts of Sokoto State, expressed solidarity with the ADC and its presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. The rally also provided an opportunity for supporters to express dissatisfaction with the Tinubu administration, particularly over the economic challenges confronting Nigerians and persistent security concerns affecting communities across the country. The development highlighted the ADC’s efforts to strengthen its support base in Sokoto State and mobilise grassroots support ahead of the 2027 general elections. As the party intensifies its nationwide mobilisation, the rally offered a platform for opposition supporters to communicate their grievances and demand political change. However, as of the time of filing this report, the ADC presidential campaign train was yet to arrive at the venue from the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, reportedly due to the large crowd along the route. item.title: 2027: No coalition needed in Ondo, APC elders declare
item.description: Target one million votes for Tinubu, 80% turnout By Dayo Johnson, Akure The PBAT Mandate Elders Forum (PMF), Ondo State chapter, has declared that there is no need for a coalition arrangement in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the All Progressives Congress (APC) is strong enough to win all elective positions. The Forum also set a target of at least one million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, alongside an 80 per cent voter turnout in the state. The position was made known at a meeting of the Forum in Akure, the state capital, where its chairman, Hon. Demola Ijabiyi, said the APC’s dominance in the state made any arrangement requiring it to surrender candidates or constituencies unnecessary. Ijabiyi said the Forum recognised the importance of cooperation among political parties with shared political objectives but maintained that such arrangements must reflect the political realities of individual states. “In Ondo State, the APC is the dominant political party, controlling government at both the state and local government levels,” he said. He said the Forum welcomed support from other political parties for Tinubu’s re-election but would not accept any arrangement that required APC candidates to step down. “Support for the President need not depend on displacing APC candidates. We have confidence in our candidates and their prospects of victory,” he said. According to him, coalition arrangements are more appropriate in states where political parties have limited electoral strength and need to combine forces to overcome their weaknesses. He explained that parties could support stronger candidates in constituencies where they lacked sufficient electoral strength in exchange for reciprocal support elsewhere. “But we don’t have that kind of circumstance in Ondo State. There is no constituency that we cannot win. There is no constituency that we do not want to contest. We are going to win all. That is the bottom line,” he said. The Forum chairman also cited the declining political strength of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), which he described as the major opposition party in the state in the past, as another reason the APC should not surrender its electoral interests. On mobilisation, Ijabiyi said the Forum was working towards extending its structures to every ward and polling unit to mobilise voters and secure victory for Tinubu and all APC candidates. He said Ondo State’s more than two million registered voters ahead of the 2027 governorship election presented a significant electoral opportunity, adding that the challenge was to translate the figure into actual voter participation. “We have therefore set a voter turnout target of at least 80 per cent. The PMF will work towards this through sustained mobilisation and voter education. Alongside this, we must earn sufficient support to deliver at least one million votes for the President,” he said. item.title: US Midterm Voters Deliver Brutal Verdict On Trump
item.description: Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran. The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his appointments. The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump’s war with Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. “This is so incredibly exciting. We can get our country back,” Kathy Jackoway said in Texas, celebrating a win by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Trump struck a conciliatory tone despite his history of rejecting election defeats, telling The New York Times he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results. “I think the Democrats did a good job,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.” Combo image of Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (r) and President of the U.S Donald Trump (l) But he sought to distance himself from his party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.” He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the result but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration. Republican Heartland Democrats flipped seats that had long been held by Republicans, scoring breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine. In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008. In Texas, Democrats won not only a Senate seat but also the governor’s race, ending decades of Republican rule. Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curveball when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers. In the House, Democrats made gains in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had carried comfortably in 2024. item.title: Police warn politicians against destroying campaign materials
item.description: …IGP orders commissioners to arrest, prosecute offenders By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has warned politicians, political thugs and other individuals against the destruction or defacement of campaign posters, banners and billboards belonging to candidates and political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Force said offenders would be arrested and prosecuted, warning that political differences or loyalty to a particular party did not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s campaign materials. Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying the police had observed with concern growing incidents of deliberate tearing, defacement and destruction of campaign materials across the country. The statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force strongly condemns this act of political intolerance and warns political thugs, hoodlums and other mischief-makers involved to desist immediately. “For the avoidance of doubt, destroying, defacing or unlawfully removing another candidate’s campaign posters and billboards may constitute malicious damage, which is a criminal offence under applicable criminal laws, including Section 451 of the Criminal Code Act and Section 326 of the Penal Code Law, which defines the offence of mischief. “Political differences or loyalty to a particular party do not give anyone the right to destroy another candidate’s property or infringe on their right to campaign freely. “The Force reiterates that all political parties and candidates, irrespective of their affiliation or status, are entitled to equal protection under the law. “No individual or group has the right to determine whose campaign materials should be displayed or destroyed.” The police said the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, had directed commissioners of police in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to take proactive measures to prevent such incidents. He also directed them to investigate reported cases and ensure that anyone found culpable was arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law. The statement added that political sponsors and individuals who recruited, encouraged or facilitated the destruction of campaign materials would also be held accountable where evidence established their involvement. The Force urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct their campaigns peacefully and respect the rights of others. It warned that political intolerance, intimidation and criminal conduct must not be allowed to undermine the democratic process. “The Nigeria Police Force will not allow political thugs and troublemakers to turn the nation’s political environment into a theatre of lawlessness. Those who choose to break the law will face the full consequences of their actions. “Be warned. Respect the law. Let democracy thrive,” the statement added. item.title: State Police Bill to reach Tinubu for assent today — Reps
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja ABUJA — The State Police Bill, seeking to decentralise policing responsibilities between the Federal and state governments, will be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday for assent. The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, disclosed this while presiding over plenary, following the approval of the proposed constitutional amendment by 29 of the 36 State Houses of Assembly. Kalu expressed excitement over the endorsement of the proposed police reform by more than two-thirds of the state legislatures, describing the development as a major step towards the establishment of state police in Nigeria. “The State Police Bill has received the backing of 29 State Assemblies. Later today, the Clerk to the National Assembly will transmit it to the President for assent,” he said. The approval by the state assemblies marks a significant milestone in efforts to amend the Constitution to allow states to establish and manage their own police forces alongside the Nigeria Police Force. The proposed reform is aimed at addressing concerns over Nigeria’s centralised policing structure, which critics argue limits the capacity of security agencies to respond effectively to local security challenges. Under the proposed arrangement, state governments would have greater responsibility for policing within their jurisdictions, while the Federal Government would retain its own police structure. The reform is expected to allow states to develop policing strategies tailored to their security needs, with the aim of strengthening intelligence gathering, community-based security and responses to crime. The transmission of the bill to the President marks the next stage in the constitutional amendment process, following its passage by the National Assembly and approval by the required number of state legislatures. The proposed establishment of state police has remained a major issue in Nigeria’s security reform debate, with supporters advocating decentralised policing as a means of improving security management across the country. item.title: UNICEF commends Taraba over education reforms
item.description: … As state launches Learning Passport in 50 pilot schools By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has commended the Taraba State Government for its education reforms, particularly the introduction of free and compulsory basic and secondary education, abolition of illegal school fees and distribution of free learning materials. The commendation was given by UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Bauchi, Dr Nuzhat Rafique, during the official launch of the Nigeria Learning Passport (NLP) in Jalingo. Rafique, who was represented by the Education Officer, UNICEF Bauchi Field Office, Raphael Aiyedipe, said the state’s education policies had contributed to an increase in school enrolment from approximately 760,000 to more than one million pupils since the inception of the current administration. She also applauded the government for promoting inclusive education for children with special needs, while strengthening teacher recruitment and professional development. According to her, the rollout of the digital learning platform was made possible through partnerships with Microsoft, the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), Airtel, IHS Towers and TECNO. She explained that the programme was designed to address connectivity barriers, reduce the number of out-of-school children and ensure continuity of learning, particularly in vulnerable communities. In his address, Governor Agbu Kefas reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to making education accessible to every child in the state, describing it as a cornerstone of sustainable development and national progress. Kefas, who was represented by the Head of Service, Dr Hamidu Kara, said the Nigeria Learning Passport represented a major step towards ensuring that no child was left behind in the state’s educational development. “The Nigerian Learning Passport represents a bold step forward in our commitment to ensure that no child is left behind in their educational journey, especially in these challenging times,” he said. He explained that the digital platform would provide flexible, accessible and inclusive learning opportunities, particularly for children affected by crises or disruptions to conventional schooling. The governor added that the initiative aligned with his administration’s free education agenda and urged stakeholders, teachers and students to embrace and promote the platform. Also speaking, the Commissioner for Secondary, Technical and Vocational Education, Dr Augustina Godwin, announced that the pilot phase of the programme would commence in 50 schools across the state. She assured that the government would expand the initiative to more schools to enable additional students to benefit from the digital learning platform. item.title: Voter Register: INEC to purge 1.5 million irregular registrants
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC is set to delete about 1.5 million voter registrations found to be irregular from the national register ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while receiving a delegation on a courtesy visit to the Commission’s headquarters. The delegation was led by the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General for West Africa and the Sahel and Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel (UNOWAS), Mr. Leonardo Santos Simão. Amupitan said technology-enabled verification helped the Commission isolate the affected entries. The deletions, he explained, are part of a comprehensive cleaning of the register through the claims and objections process. The final register is scheduled for publication on December 15, 2026. The INEC chairman said the Commission has registered approximately 103 million voters. Young Nigerians aged 18 to 34 make up nearly 29 per cent of them. He added that the distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) is ongoing across the country. Amupitan said INEC would continue to strengthen the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) for accreditation, and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) for public access to polling-unit results. The Commission is also planning a mock accreditation and election exercise to test these tools, identify possible challenges and build public confidence before the 2027 polls. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation as major threats to electoral integrity. He warned that the growing misuse of artificial intelligence and coordinated online campaigns could undermine public confidence in the electoral system. He therefore asked the UN for stronger collaboration on information integrity, countering electoral disinformation and public awareness. Other areas of prospective cooperation he outlined include conflict prevention, election security, early-warning mechanisms, stakeholder dialogue and peacebuilding. He also listed the protection of vulnerable groups, particularly women, youths and persons with disabilities. On security, Amupitan said INEC is working with relevant agencies to map areas vulnerable to electoral violence and other threats, so that preventive measures can be developed. Simão said the visit was meant to show UN support for INEC, noting that the Commission carries a significant responsibility in managing elections in a country confronted by terrorism and other security challenges. According to him, the UN will maintain a presence during the elections, not as observers since it has no mandate for election observation, but to encourage positive conduct and support an atmosphere conducive to peaceful participation. item.title: Kidnappers free six Benue mourners after N2.5m ransom
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The six mourners, including a bereaved man, who were abducted while conveying the corpse of his late wife from Kano State to Okpoga, headquarters of Okpokwu Local Government Area (LGA) of Benue State, have regained their freedom after spending several days in captivity. The victims were reportedly released by their abductors around 11pm on Tuesday after a ransom of N2.5 million was paid. A community member, Meddy Olotu, who disclosed this, said the kidnappers also demanded 10 plates of food as part of the conditions for releasing the victims. The six mourners, comprising the deceased woman’s husband and five other persons accompanying him, were kidnapped along Adoka Road in Otukpo LGA at about 8pm last Friday. They were reportedly transporting the woman’s corpse from Kano State to Okpoga for burial when they were intercepted by gunmen, who subsequently abandoned the corpse inside their vehicle. The abductors had initially demanded N15 million ransom for the release of the six victims. Confirming their release, Olotu said the victims regained their freedom after the ransom was paid and the food demand met. “They were released by their captors around 11pm Tuesday night after a ransom of N2.5 million was paid for their release. “Additionally, the captors also requested that when the ransom is being delivered, 10 plates of food should be brought to them. That was done and they have all regained their freedom,” he said. Olotu added that the victims were receiving medical attention after allegedly suffering torture and physical abuse while in captivity. “As I speak, they are receiving medical treatment because they were severely tortured and manhandled, so they need medical attention,” he said. The Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area, Maxwell Ogiri, also confirmed the release of the abducted mourners on Tuesday night. However, efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for confirmation and further details were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report. item.title: Don’t politicise national security, TMS warns Atiku as DSS probes Sokoto protest
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation otherwise known as Tinubu Must Stay TMS has warned former Vice President Atiku Abubakar against politicising national security, as the Department of State Services DSS investigates his allegation that it mobilised protesters to disrupt campaign activities in Sokoto State. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, made the accusation against the DSS. The agency denied it, but said its Director General had ordered an investigation. In a statement signed by TMS’ Director of Strategic Communication, Adebisi Adams, the group said claims involving security institutions must be backed by proof and tested through an impartial inquiry. TMS Director General, Marcel Ngogbehei, acknowledged the right of political leaders to scrutinise public institutions and demand accountability. He cautioned, however, against dragging sensitive security matters into partisan contests through allegations that have not been substantiated. “These are serious accusations. They deserve credible evidence, due process and an impartial investigation,” Ngogbehei said. According to him, national security should not be reduced to an instrument of partisan advantage. He said Atiku, as a former Vice President and prominent national figure, should appreciate the potential consequences of grave allegations against institutions entrusted with protecting lives and maintaining national security. TMS drew attention to the DSS account of an incident involving the Sokoto ADC governorship candidate, Mannir Daniya, on 31 October 2026. According to the DSS, its operatives evacuated Daniya to safety after he came under attack, while two of its personnel were assaulted and required hospital treatment. The DSS added that Daniya later contacted its Sokoto State Director to express appreciation and ask for additional reinforcement. Their professionalism, independence and credibility must not become casualties of political competition,” Ngogbehei said.
